envelope.text: - There is no `ok()`: the value has no shutdown state; liveness is the

why:
phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `env` joined the measured feature set (`scripts/api_parity/extract_rust.py`, `NROS_FEATURES`), so this type is on the surface for the first time and correlates `same`; it read `theirs-only` before only because the extractor never compiled `src/init.rs`. The old text ("as `cpp:Context` ... neither is available to an image with no env and one session") described the invisible state and is history.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclrs::Context` (0.7.0, `rclrs/src/context.rs`) OWNS the rcl context — built from argv (`Context::new(args, options)`) or the environment (`from_env`, `default_from_env`), it parses `--ros-args`, answers `domain_id()` / `ok()`, and is the factory for executors (`create_executor`).

OURS (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs`, by name): a plain value `{domain_id, locator, mode, rmw, source}` that the free functions `nros::init()` / `init_with_args` / `init_with_launch*` return, and whose one method `config(node_name)` (by name) materialises the `ExecutorConfig` a caller hands to `Executor::open`. It owns nothing and parses nothing: it is the resolved identity, read through the one hosted resolver (`nros::env::try_resolve_hosted`, issue 0687).

Disposition ADOPT-BOUNDED. The name carries the same identity (domain, middleware selection), and `ctx.domain_id` reads where `ctx.domain_id()` did; the envelope is that construction is the free `init*` family (the argv form REFUSES `--ros-args`, see `rust:init_with_args`); `Context::default_from_env()` is the one member that maps 1:1 onto ours, `nros::init()`, and its row is a `rename`, that the executor is opened INTO caller-owned storage from `ctx.config(name)` rather than allocated by the context (RFC-0045; no allocator), and that there is no `ok()` because the value has no shutdown state — liveness is the executor's. Each missing member has its own row below, because the type is `same` and a member gap inside a shipped type is argued on its own (`lookup`'s inheritance rule). The whole module is behind `env`, which requires `std`: an embedded image never compiles it, and its identity arrives through `BootConfig` instead.

phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. The last sentence above is history: `init.rs` is out from behind `env`. `Context` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs`, by name) compiles on every target with `alloc` as its floor (`locator` and `rmw` are owned `String`s); the `env` feature gates only the process-environment reader and the argv/launch entries. The rclrs constructors exist under their names — `default_from_env` (`adopt`), `from_env` (`adopt-bounded`), hosted-only `new` (`adopt-bounded`) — each on its own row; freestanding, the first two resolve to `Context::baked()` (`rust:Context::baked`). Construction is no longer ONLY the free `init*` family; the envelope that remains is the executor being opened from `ctx.config(name)` (RFC-0045) and the absence of `ok()`.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN, and one half CORRECTED. The type's rustdoc said nothing about the missing `ok()`. And the "executor opened INTO caller-owned storage from `ctx.config(name)` rather than allocated by the context" half above is stale: `Context::create_executor` (leaks an executor-lifetime backing, `alloc`) and `Context::create_executor_in` (caller storage) now exist, so the context IS the factory for executors, as rclrs's is. What remains bounded — no `ok()`, `domain_id` a field rather than a method, the context a resolved value rather than an rcl-context owner — is now on `Context`'s rustdoc.
